notes: Slip-and-fall premises liability case on a commercial parking lot (trespasser/licensee/invitee duty analysis); the 'landlord out of possession' language concerns a commercial lease between a realty company and a retail tenant, not any household letting or lodging arrangement.

court: Westmoreland County Court of Common Pleas
notes: Social-guest injury case (duty to control conduct of guests at a Christmas Eve gathering) turning on Restatement §§315/318 licensee liability principles; no compensated occupancy or lodging/boarding arrangement is involved.

holding_summary: In a public-assistance eligibility dispute, the Commonwealth Court held that DPW improperly presumed petitioner shared all household expenses with his housemate merely because they were on a joint lease and shared a dwelling, without resolving the disputed factual question of whether petitioner instead paid Ms. Torres a fixed weekly fee as a 'roomer or roomer and boarder.' The case was vacated and remanded for factual findings on petitioner's roomer/boarder status and, if that status is not found, on what resources of the co-occupant were actually available to him.

quotes.text: A roomer or boarder, or both is one who pays a fixed fee to a provider of service for room or board, or both.

Since resolution of the factual issue of whether the petitioner was a roomer or roomer and boarder, as defined in 55 Pa. Code §171.22, is pivotal to a proper determination of this case, this case must be remanded for further factual findings.

notes: This is a welfare-benefits (assistance-unit) case, not a right-to-let or police-power-regulation dispute; it substantively defines 'roomer/boarder' (fixed fee paid for room or board) but takes no position favorable or adverse to householder letting, so polarity is left null.

holding_summary: The Commonwealth Court affirmed denial of a special exception/occupancy permit that would have allowed the owners to lawfully rent two third-floor rooms as lodgings, holding that neighbor testimony of increased traffic, lack of parking, litter, and noise from the additional roomers was substantial evidence supporting the Board's finding of detriment to the single-family residential district. The court also rejected an estoppel argument based on the owners' unchallenged years of unlawful room rental, since mere non-enforcement creates no vested right to violate zoning.

quotes.text: the proposed occupancy of third floor of a 2 1/2 story, 2 family dwelling, located in an R-1A zoning district, for two lodgers, would have a further detrimental and deleterious effect on this single family residential area.

there was over-riding testimony by neighboring owners, residents, and taxpayers that increased occupancy of the subject property in this E-1A highest class residential district was detrimental to the public health, morals; safety and general welfare of the neighborhood stemming from increased traffic, no available parking, litter, loud noises and unseemly conduct.
the order of the Court of Common Pleas of Allegheny County at No. SA 1274 of 1979, dated March 31, 1981, is affirmed.

notes: Owners rented out all of a small multi-unit building rather than occupying it themselves, so classified as commercial_operator despite modest scale (two dwelling units plus two rented rooms).

Zoning variance dispute over an automobile-repair garage; the ordinance's boarder/roomer permitted-use language is quoted only as background listing of R-M district uses and is never at issue in the case.

Zoning classification dispute over whether an eight-resident personal care home for older adults qualifies as a 'multiple-family dwelling'; concerns institutional custodial care, not compensated room/lodging letting by a householder or regulation of a boarding house.

Tax exemption dispute over a skilled nursing facility's use-and-occupancy tax, turning on the meaning of 'user or occupier' under Philadelphia's tax code; not about the legality or regulation of short-term room letting.

Large apartment complex seeking a variance from the zoning 'family' definition to permit four unrelated student co-tenants per unit (economic-hardship variance denied); a separate issue about a variance from the ordinance's 'lodgers' restriction was raised but expressly not reached by the court and remanded, so there is no lodging-related holding to record.

Fire-code sprinkler dispute over a shopping-center basement classified as 'mercantile occupancy'; the opinion cites Queenside Hills Realty Co. v. Saxl (a New York lodging-house sprinkler case) only as background precedent on the police power, but the actual property and dispute here is a commercial retail building, not a lodging or boarding house.

court: Dauphin County Court of Common Pleas
notes: Dispute over whether a monthly parking-lot fee creates a lease or a license; concerns parking privileges only, no dwelling, room, or lodging occupancy is at issue.

court: Lackawanna County Court of Common Pleas
notes: Charitable maternity home for pregnant women/teens held to qualify as a 'family' rather than a 'rooming house' under Scranton's zoning ordinance; the court expressly found no profit motive in the arrangement, so this does not bear on compensated letting or commercial boarding-house regulation.

quotes.text: Strauss testified that three students live in each house and each student has her own bedroom.
despite the fact that the tenants paid for their lodging and some were temporary lodgers, the residents functioned as a family

notes: Landlord owned and rented three separate houses under township rental-registration permits rather than occupying any of them, so classified as commercial_operator; the letting arrangement (individually-let bedrooms sharing common kitchen/bath) closely parallels the boarding/lodging fact pattern even though the court resolved it under a zoning 'family' definition rather than lease/license doctrine.

Variance dispute over installing a second kitchen for a related family (kosher food preparation) in a single-family dwelling; concerns the 'one kitchen per dwelling unit' zoning rule for a related family, not letting or lodging of any kind.

court: Mercer County Court of Common Pleas
notes: Dispute over the meaning of a life-estate/reservation agreement's phrase 'continue to occupy' as applied to a widow's right to remain in and collect rents from an apartment building she inherited under a will; concerns occupancy/domicile interpretation for the beneficiary herself, not compensated lodging of a third party.

Eminent domain case computing special dislocation damages owed to the owner of a condemned rental apartment building; the dispute is over the statutory damages formula (owner-occupant vs. tenant vs. non-displaced landlord), not the legality or regulation of letting rooms/dwellings.

Baseball stadium spectator injury case; the passing reference to a lessor-out-of-possession's duty to lessee's invitees concerns a commercial stadium sublease, unrelated to household or lodging occupancy.

First Amendment challenge to Penn State's regulation of door-to-door canvassing in university residence-hall living areas; the treatment of dorm hallways as 'private living quarters' arises in a free-speech/state-action context involving institutional student housing, not compensated householder letting or boarding-house police-power regulation.

Zoning parking-space dispute for a proposed supermarket; the ordinance's 'Rooming House Dwelling' parking-space provision is quoted only as one line of a comprehensive parking schedule and is never applied to the facts of this case.
